title: The Portrait of the Marlowe Estate
premise: Isandro Eriksen, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made her the unofficial archivist of Marlowe's secrets, receives two letters on the same morning: one confessing to a fire that killed three people at the Marlowe Estate twenty years ago, and one promising a second confession if she can find 'the ledger painted in plain sight.' Following the letters into the decaying estate—now slated for demolition by the powerful Calloway family—she discovers the mansion's famous murals encode a financial ledger documenting decades of blackmail, embezzlement, and bought silence. As Isandro decodes the paintings with the help of Wren, the estate's last caretaker and the fire's orphaned survivor, she realizes her own late mother was one of the conspirators, and that the second letter-writer is killing off everyone who could still testify. In the end, Isandro must choose between exposing the truth and protecting Wren—the one person who feels like family—ultimately broadcasting the decoded ledger from the estate itself as it burns a second time, letting duty to the dead finally yield to love for the living.
about_author: August Dunmore is the pen name of a former insurance fraud examiner who spent eleven years in New England claims departments before turning to fiction. Dunmore writes mysteries about paper trails, small towns, and the people who remember everything.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Morning
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On an ordinary Tuesday, Isandro files claims with perfect recall until two letters arrive: a confession to the 2004 Marlowe Estate fire, unsigned, and a second note reading 'Find the ledger painted in plain sight. You have until the equinox.' The beat is cold curiosity cracking open old dread.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets on Purpose
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She walks Marlowe's main street, testing neighbors' memories against her own flawless ones, and finds the town's amnesia about the fire too coordinated to be natural. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being the only person who cannot choose what to forget.

chapters.title: A House Scheduled to Die
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She visits the condemned Marlowe Estate, scheduled for demolition by Calloway Development, and meets Wren Ashby, the young caretaker who refuses to leave. Beat: instant, wary recognition between two people guarding the same ruin.

chapters.title: What the Murals Are Hiding
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Studying photographs she took of the ballroom murals, Isandro notices recurring numbers disguised as decorative motifs—dates, sums, initials. Beat: the thrill of the hunt, and the first vertigo of realizing the confession letter may be true.

chapters.title: The Fire, As Filed
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with flashback texture. She pulls her own seven-year-old claim file on the fire: three deaths, ruled accidental, settled quietly by an insurer now defunct. Beat: professional unease hardening into personal obsession.

chapters.title: Wren's Version
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The caretaker reveals she was the fire's orphaned survivor, raised by the estate's housekeeper, and that someone has been leaving fresh flowers in the burned east wing. Beat: grief offered like a key.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro maps every secret she has ever memorized about Marlowe's leading families, looking for patterns intersecting the mural numbers. Beat: the burden of memory becoming a weapon.

chapters.title: The First Name Crossed Out
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Former mayor Aldous Pike—the man who signed the fire permit waivers—is found drowned in his own koi pond, a paint chip in his fist. Beat: the promise of 'more' arriving as murder.

chapters.title: Calloway's Welcome
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Vivienne Calloway, matriarch of the development empire buying the estate, invites Isandro to lunch and offers her a generous consulting fee to 'wrap up loose ends.' Beat: charm as threat; power showing its teeth.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren shows Isandro the conservatory frescoes where botanical illustrations hide account entries—payments routed through the estate's charitable trust. Beat: wonder and horror braided together.

chapters.title: My Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A ledger entry bears her mother Margit's initials; Margit was the estate's bookkeeper before the fire and died when Isandro was nineteen. Beat: betrayal reordering a lifetime of grief.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Favors
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Reconstructing memories, Isandro realizes the anonymous tips that built her career all steered her away from Marlowe. Someone curated her blindness. Beat: paranoia blooming in fertile ground.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Box
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren opens her guardian's hidden box: a half-burned photograph of five people, including Margit Eriksen and a young Vivienne Calloway, standing before the unfinished murals. Beat: tenderness curdling into shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Equinox Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Decoding the mural dates, Isandro finds they count down to the autumn equinox—the demolition date—and that each entry corresponds to a person. Three are already dead. Beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: An Insurance Man's Ghost
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She tracks down retired adjuster Hollis Brandt, who handled the original fire claim and now lives in fear behind new locks. He confirms the fire was arson-for-hire but refuses to testify. Beat: cowardice witnessed without contempt.

chapters.title: Dinner With the Enemy
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the Calloway gala, Vivienne probes Isandro's investigation while her son Theo—charming, restless—warns her privately that his mother keeps a room he's never been allowed to enter. Beat: attraction and danger wearing the same face.

chapters.title: The Room Behind the Mural
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following proportions in the frescoes, Wren and Isandro find a concealed study containing the trust's original books and Margit's coded correspondence. Beat: triumph immediately shadowed by footsteps above.

chapters.title: Margit's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the hidden study, Isandro reads her mother's unsent confession: Margit kept the ledger as leverage to protect her daughter, not to profit. Beat: love against duty, inherited across a grave.

chapters.title: Hollis Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Hollis Brandt fails to meet her and is found dead of 'natural causes,' his files incinerated. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve—her questions are getting people killed.

chapters.title: Theo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo offers Isandro access to his mother's private records in exchange for taking him along when the truth breaks; he wants out of the family machine. Beat: alliance formed in mutual self-interest, edged with real feeling.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Version of Love
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. The matriarch reflects on the fire she commissioned to erase the trust's debts, and on Margit, the friend she betrayed. Beat: the antagonist rendered human without absolution—power corrupting even its own affections.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Writer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Handwriting analysis points Isandro toward the confessor's identity: someone inside the original conspiracy who has begun eliminating the others. Beat: the hunter realizing there are two hunters.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fraying
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Isandro's partnership deepens over long nights of decoding—shared meals in the caretaker's cottage, jokes, quiet trust—until Isandro hides a page to protect Wren. Beat: intimacy damaged by protection, the book's central theme made personal.

chapters.title: The Page I Kept
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The hidden page names Wren's parents as the arsonists, hired and then betrayed. Isandro must decide whether Wren learning the truth will break or free her. Beat: dread of honesty.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Conservatory
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds the withheld page and confronts Isandro; fury gives way to a harder bond—they choose each other knowing the worst. Beat: rupture and repair; found family forged in fire's aftermath.

chapters.title: Theo's Mistake
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo copies his mother's records but is caught; Vivienne, coldly loving, gives him one chance to prove loyalty by delivering Isandro. Beat: the son cornered between blood and conscience.

chapters.title: The Confessor Revealed
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro identifies the letter writer: Corliss Dane, the estate's former groundskeeper and the fire's actual hand, now dying of cancer and cleansing the world before he goes—including, perhaps, himself. Beat: pity entangled with terror.

chapters.title: A Meeting With a Dying Man
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Corliss confesses fully: Vivienne ordered the fire; Margit's ledger was the insurance policy that kept Vivienne paying hush money for twenty years. Beat: truth delivered like a relay baton.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Demolition crews arrive early; Vivienne moves up the schedule, having learned about the hidden study. Wren and Isandro have one night to copy and verify everything. Beat: breathless urgency, working by lamplight among ghosts.

chapters.title: The Demolition Order
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro attempts legal injunctions and press calls; every channel is owned, delayed, or bought. Beat: the machinery of power shown closing ranks.

chapters.title: What Theo Chose
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ordered to betray Isandro, Theo instead delivers his mother's private safe contents to the cottage—then disappears, phone going dark. Beat: sacrifice without guarantee.

chapters.title: Smoke Before Fire
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Smoke rises from the east wing at dawn; someone is burning the evidence ahead of the wrecking balls. Wren runs in; Isandro follows. Beat: panic, heat, the past literally aflame.

chapters.title: Inside the Burning Wing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro drags Wren out through the servant's corridor her mother once described, memorizing the final ledger pages in the smoke because there is no time to carry them. Beat: photographic memory as salvation; near-death clarity.

chapters.title: Corliss's Last Canvas
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They find Corliss dead in the conservatory, an finished confession beside him naming Vivienne outright—he set the diversionary fire to buy them time. Beat: the confessor's redemption, costly and incomplete.

chapters.title: Vivienne at the Gate
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Confronted amid the demolition, Vivienne offers Isandro everything—money, erasure, Wren's safety—in exchange for silence, invoking their mothers' friendship. Beat: temptation articulated perfectly enough to be frightening.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro weighs the offer against duty to the dead and love for Wren, and understands her mother kept the ledger not for justice but for leverage—she can do better. Beat: the thematic fulcrum; decision made.

chapters.title: Broadcast From the Ruins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Using the estate's ancient transmitter and Theo's recovered records, Isandro reads the decoded ledger live online as the walls come down around her. Beat: climax—truth spoken aloud in the place built to bury it.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. State investigators, freed from local ownership, arrest Vivienne; the town's forgetting finally cracks into remembering. Beat: justice arriving imperfect, partial, real.

chapters.title: What Remains Standing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The estate is preserved as a memorial and archive; Wren, offered the curatorship, asks Isandro to stay—not as investigator, but as family. Beat: tenderness after wreckage.

chapters.title: The Portrait We Keep
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Closing the case file she never opened under her own name, Isandro hangs the restored mural portrait of the five conspirators beside a new photograph: herself, Wren, and Theo on the cottage steps. Beat: resolution—memory chosen freely at last, love recorded where duty used to live.
